2026_348_3c_draft_boe_tsd_athletic_handb.paragraph: Presented to the Troy School District Board of Education as agenda item 3C on April 21, 2026, the draft Athletic Handbook for Students, revised Spring 2026, sets out eligibility, conduct, and discipline rules for all district student-athletes under MHSAA regulations and the district Student Code of Conduct. It runs 27 numbered pages across fifteen sections covering enrollment and age limits, FinalForms registration, academic eligibility, awards, amateur status, attendance, the TROY CAP PACT, transportation, substance-use discipline, Name-Image-Likeness activity, and appeals. Its most consequential addition is a four-level disciplinary framework with a percentage-based suspension model tied to MHSAA minimums.
2026_348_3c_draft_boe_tsd_athletic_handb.page:
**Document**
Athletic Handbook for Students, Troy School District, Revised Spring 2026. Board of Education draft, agenda item 3C, meeting of April 21, 2026. Fifteen sections, paginated -1- through -27-. Policies marked with an asterisk are Troy School District policies that also align with MHSAA regulations.

**Section I - Eligibility**
Students must be enrolled by the Monday of the fourth week of the semester in which they compete and must reside in and attend the school they represent; students at TCCHS and IA East compete at their home school by residency. High school participants must be under nineteen (19); a nineteenth birthday on or after September 1 preserves eligibility for the balance of the year. Seventh and eighth graders must be under fourteen (14) and fifteen (15) respectively. All registration runs through FinalForms, including the CAP PACT Agreement, Application to Participate, Pay to Participate Agreement (paid before the first competition), Athletics Transportation Agreement, Concussion Awareness form, and MHSAA Acknowledgement of Risk; paper submissions are no longer accepted. Physicals must be completed by an M.D., D.O., physician assistant, or nurse practitioner and dated on or after April 15 of the previous school year. MHSAA limits competition to four (4) seasons per sport in grades 9-12 and four (4) first and four (4) second semesters of eligibility; grades 7-8 are unlimited.

**Academic Standards**
| Setting | Standard |
|---|---|
| District baseline | Passing credit in a minimum of five (5) classes the previous semester |
| Troy College and Career High School | Pass 7 of 8 classes over the previous two semesters |
| Intersect and Inspire High School | Pass 5 of 6 classes over the previous two semesters |
| International Academy | Pass 7 of 8 classes the previous semester |
| Middle school | Pass 5 of 6 classes the previous quarter |

Eligibility is reviewed at the end of each marking period (every 10 weeks); ineligibility runs no less than one full calendar week, Monday through Sunday. Deficiencies from a prior semester carry a minimum sixty (60) scheduled school days of ineligibility. New transfers get one transitional semester at the MHSAA minimum of four (4) passing classes.

**Sections II-XIII**
Awards may not exceed a fair market value of twenty-five dollars ($25.00); violations bring at least one semester of ineligibility. Amateur status bars pay for play, paid officiating, and professional contracts across sixteen listed MHSAA sports, with reinstatement possible only after one full school year. Outside competition in the same sport during the season costs a minimum of two (2) contests at middle school and three (3) at high school. Full-day school attendance is required to participate. Attendance expectations are tiered across middle school, freshman, junior varsity, and varsity, with religious and cultural observances automatically excused. Section VII contains the TROY CAP PACT (Coach-Athlete-Parent) and a grievance ladder: informal contact allowing the coach two (2) school days, Level 1 written complaint answered within five (5) school days, Level 2 to the building Athletic Coordinator answered within seven (7) school days, Level 3 with the building principal and District Athletic Director. Transportation violations cost the next contest, then possible removal. Section XII permits Name, Image, and Likeness activity, called Personal Branding Activity by MHSAA, only outside school time and without school marks, collectives, or booster involvement.

**Substance and Discipline**
High school substance violations are cumulative across a career: first tobacco/nicotine violation is 1 contest or 1 week, not to exceed 10% of the regular season; first alcohol/drug or second tobacco violation is 2 contests or 2 weeks, not to exceed 20%; the next step is removal for the season and ineligibility for the first 50% of the next season; then a 365-day suspension; then permanent loss of eligibility. Middle school violators are removed from the team immediately. The Section XIV framework grades misconduct as Level I (0%, coach-managed), Level II (10-20% of contests), Level III (20-40%), and Level IV (removal, 50-100% of the season). Appeals go in writing to the building principal or athletic coordinator within five (5) school days, with a meeting in two (2) school days and a written decision in two (2) school days; further appeal goes to the district Director of Athletics within two (2) school days. MHSAA eligibility and transfer appeals are separate and final at the state level.
2026_348_3c_draft_boe_tsd_athletic_handb.verbose:
The Troy School District Athletic Handbook for Students, revised Spring 2026, was submitted to the Board of Education as draft agenda item 3C for the meeting of April 21, 2026. The handbook spans fifteen sections over 27 numbered pages and integrates Michigan High School Athletic Association (MHSAA) rules as adopted by the district with district-specific interscholastic policies. It operates under the umbrella of the Troy School District Student Code of Conduct, is in effect throughout the entire year including all seasons of practice and competition, and marks with an asterisk those policies that align with MHSAA regulations. A student-athlete ruled academically ineligible for contests or scrimmages may still practice provided they are not under school suspension, though inability to compete may affect award eligibility under team-specific requirements set by the coach.

Section I, Rules of Eligibility for Participation, requires enrollment by the Monday of the fourth week of the semester of competition, residence within the boundaries of the school attended, and enrollment in the school for which the student competes. Students attending TCCHS and IA East must participate in athletics at their home school based on residency. Under paragraph B, high school students in grades nine through twelve must be under nineteen (19) years of age, with a nineteenth birthday on or after September 1 of the current school year preserving eligibility for the balance of the year; seventh and eighth graders must be under fourteen (14) and fifteen (15) years of age respectively, with the same September 1 rule. Paragraph C requires a parent/guardian and student FinalForms account, the district designated digital platform for athletic clearance, including complete parent and student accounts, all electronic forms and agreements, a current physical form dated after April 15 of the previous school year, and a completed health history and medical profile. Families must read and acknowledge the Athletic Handbook for Student-Athletes, the CAP PACT Agreement form, the Application to Participate form, the Pay to Participate Agreement (paid before the first competition), the Athletics Transportation Agreement form, the Concussion Awareness form, and the MHSAA Acknowledgement of Risk form. Records are stored in FinalForms and accessible to coaches, athletic trainers, the building athletic coordinator, and the district athletic director; paper submissions are no longer accepted.

Paragraph D requires an athletics physical examination by a physician (M.D. or D.O.), physician assistant, or nurse practitioner, dated on or after April 15 of the previous school year, submitted electronically on the MHSAA physical form. Paragraph E limits students to four (4) seasons of interscholastic competition in a specific sport in grades 9 through 12, distributed as no more than four first semesters and four second semesters, with no more than one season per sport per school year even where a sport such as bowling or tennis is offered twice; fall sideline cheer does not count as a competition season against winter competitive cheer. Grades 7 and 8 are not limited in seasons. Paragraph F caps eligibility at four (4) first semesters and four (4) second semesters in grades 9 through 12, with enrollment by the Monday of the fourth week or participation in one or more contests constituting a full semester; high school semesters must be consecutive.

Paragraph G sets academic eligibility. The MHSAA and district baseline requires passing grades (credit) in a minimum of five (5) classes in the previous semester. Troy College and Career High School students must pass at least seven (7) of eight (8) classes over the previous two semesters; Intersect and Inspire High School students at least five (5) of six (6) over the previous two semesters; International Academy students seven (7) of eight (8) in the previous semester; middle school students five (5) of six (6) in the previous quarter. Eligibility is formally reviewed at the end of each marking period (every 10 weeks). A student failing a quarterly grade check becomes ineligible for competition and may regain eligibility through a weekly academic progress report, with ineligibility lasting no less than one full calendar week (Monday through Sunday), a rule that also applies to the MHSAA 60-Day Rule. Deficiencies tied to the previous semester carry a minimum of sixty (60) scheduled school days of ineligibility in the current semester. Transfer students new to the district receive one transitional semester during which they must meet the MHSAA minimum of passing four (4) classes. Middle school student-athletes in grades 7-8 must pass at least five of six classes each marking period, with weekly progress monitoring for those who fall below.

Section II, Awards, permits symbolic or merchandise awards not exceeding a fair market value of twenty-five dollars ($25.00), plus banquets, luncheons and dinners, non-competitive trips, and spectator admission to non-Troy School District events accepted in kind. Cash, merchandise certificates, negotiable financial documents, and memberships, privileges, services, athletic equipment, apparel or jewelry above the $25 limit are prohibited, as is acceptance of an award on a student-athlete's behalf by a parent, relative or friend before high school graduation. Violation brings ineligibility for at least one semester from the date of the violation; a violation after the fourth Monday of a semester costs the remainder of that semester and the entire next semester.

Section III, Maintaining Amateur Status, bars accepting money or valuable consideration for athletic participation (separate from permissible Name, Image and Likeness activity), receiving compensation for officiating interscholastic contests, and signing a contract or agreement to play or try out with a professional team. The rule applies to MHSAA-sponsored baseball, basketball, cross country, football, golf, gymnastics, soccer, softball, skiing, tennis, track and field, volleyball, wrestling, ice hockey, competitive cheer, and swimming and diving. Instructional fees or pay for coaching youth or recreational sports may be allowed if unconnected to interscholastic athletics. Violators are ineligible and may not apply to the MHSAA for reinstatement until one full school year has passed.

Section IV, Outside of School Athletic Competition, prohibits non-school club, AAU, travel or rec competition in the same sport during the season once a student has practiced, tried out, scrimmaged or competed for a school team. Middle school violators are ineligible for a minimum of the next two (2) contests or dates of competition, high school for a minimum of the next three (3), with ineligibility extending up to the remainder of the season. The Limited Team Membership provision sets a minimum of the next three (3) days of competition and a maximum of the remainder of the season. Students may not participate in all-star contests in an MHSAA-sponsored sport during the school year. These rules reflect Section 12(A) - Limited Team Membership of the MHSAA handbook.

Section V requires a student to be in school for the full instructional day to participate that day. Excused absences include illness with documentation, medical or dental appointments with verification, court appearances, religious observances, bereavement or family emergencies, and pre-approved college visits or academic travel, with extenuating circumstances approved by the building principal or designee. Unexcused absences, including skipping class, oversleeping, leaving campus without permission, and failure to document, render a student ineligible that day, and participation anyway is a Code of Conduct violation. Section VI addresses attendance at practices and contests, listing excused categories including religious holidays and cultural observances, which the district states will be automatically excused without penalty when the coach is notified in advance. Unexcused absences may bring reduced playing time, loss of leadership roles, and team consequences. Level-based expectations are stated separately for middle school (grades 7-8), freshman level (primarily 9th grade), junior varsity (JV/JVA), and varsity, each repeating that school-day attendance is required and that cultural and religious observances are honored.

Section VII sets season expectations by level with distinct philosophies: middle school focuses on skill development and playing time for all when possible; the freshman/JV B level introduces merit-based playing time and a shift from equal play to earned play; junior varsity/JVA (9th-11th grades) prepares athletes for varsity demands; varsity represents competitive excellence with playing time earned. The section contains the TROY CAP PACT (Coach-Athlete-Parent PACT), which all student-athletes, parents and coaches must review and sign before each season through FinalForms, enumerating the coach's expectations of parents (nine items), parents' expectations of the coach (six items), the coach's expectations of the athlete (fourteen items), the athlete's expectations of the coach (ten items), and the athlete's expectations of parents (six items). A complaint/grievance policy follows: the athlete first speaks with the coach; informally the parent then contacts the coach and allows two (2) school days for a response and possible face-to-face meeting; Level 1 is a written concern to the coach with a written reply within five (5) school days; Level 2 is a written disagreement to the building Athletic Coordinator within five (5) school days with the Level 1 response attached, an independent investigation, and a written reply within seven (7) school days; Level 3 is a meeting with the Building Principal and District Athletic Director. Complaints alleging a potential criminal act or immoral behavior by a coach begin at Level 2.

Section VIII requires travel with the team on district-provided transportation, whether school-owned, chartered or otherwise approved. Students may leave a contest site with a parent, legal guardian, or adult family member only with prior written permission through FinalForms and advance coach approval. Where district transportation is not used, the coach must document departure with a signed sign-out form or approved sign-off list. A first violation makes the student ineligible for the next scheduled contest while still practicing; a second may bring removal from the team for the season. Section IX makes student-athletes financially responsible for uniforms and equipment lost, abused, damaged through negligence, or not returned, suspending future season participation and withholding awards, letters and recognitions until resolved.

Section X prohibits use, possession, sale or distribution of tobacco and nicotine products including vaping devices, alcohol, marijuana, non-prescribed controlled substances, look-alike substances, banned performance-enhancing drugs or supplements as defined by the NCAA and Michigan Department of Health, prescription medication not prescribed to the student, and misuse of over-the-counter medication, at all times on and off school grounds year-round. Middle school violators are immediately removed from the team, with reinstatement considered only after a meeting with the student, parent/guardian and building administrator. High school consequences are cumulative from the first day of participation as a freshman: a first tobacco/nicotine violation brings a minimum 1 contest or 1 week suspension, whichever is greater, not to exceed 10% of the regular season, an optional educational workshop at family cost, and possible parent conference; a first alcohol/drug violation or second tobacco violation brings a minimum 2 contests or 2 weeks, not to exceed 20% of the regular season, a mandatory parent meeting with coach and building administrator, and a required substance education or intervention program at family cost, with missed games carrying over to the next season; a second alcohol/drug or third tobacco violation brings immediate removal for the current season and, if less than 50% of the season remains, ineligibility for the first 50% of the next season plus a professional assessment from a Michigan Department of Health-approved provider at family cost; a third alcohol/drug or fourth tobacco violation brings suspension from all athletic participation for 365 days from the date of the confirmed violation; a fourth alcohol/drug or fifth tobacco violation brings permanent loss of athletic eligibility in the Troy School District. In-season violations apply immediately; out-of-season violations are enforced at the start of the next season of participation, even in the next school year.

Section XI makes summer and off-season camps, clinics and conditioning strictly voluntary, and per MHSAA regulations prohibits requiring off-season participation as a condition of making a team, earning a roster spot, receiving playing time, or level placement. Section XII permits Name, Image, and Likeness activity, termed Personal Branding Activities by the MHSAA, only when independent of school teams, not tied to athletic performance or team success, outside school time and away from school facilities and events, and compliant with MHSAA rules. Prohibited are use of school names, logos, uniforms, mascots or facilities, implying school, district or MHSAA endorsement, pay-for-play, agreements arranged by coaches, school personnel or booster organizations, collectives or group NIL agreements, and promotion of products violating school policy. Agreements must be reported per MHSAA requirements before participation; the district, coaches and staff provide no legal, tax or contract guidance; NIL may not be used to influence enrollment, transfer or team placement.

Section XIII allows sport-specific supplemental rules developed by coaches and approved by the building athletic coordinator and building principal or designee, with athlete-specific plans or behavior contracts approved by the building athletic coordinator or Director of Athletics; all supplemental rules must be written and distributed at the start of the season. A student suspended from school is ineligible for practices and contests during the suspension; an academically ineligible student may practice at the coach's discretion; a student dismissed for the season forfeits team awards and varsity letters.

Section XIV establishes the Student-Athlete Handbook Disciplinary Framework, aligned with MHSAA and National Federation of State High School Associations (NFHS) standards, with the district Code of Conduct taking precedence in any conflict. Level I minor violations (tardiness, dress code, non-directed inappropriate language, failure to follow team procedures) draw warnings, parent communication, temporary reduction in playing time, team consequences, and restorative conversation. Level II moderate violations (repeated Level I, disrespect, minor unsportsmanlike conduct, social media misuse) draw suspension from contests (1-3 or a defined percentage), parent conference, behavioral contract, and removal from leadership roles. Level III major violations (insubordination, ejection per MHSAA/NFHS rules, bullying, harassment or hazing, substance use, academic dishonesty) draw multi-contest suspension aligned with MHSAA minimums, temporary removal from team activities, mandatory parent conference, educational interventions, and probation. Level IV severe violations (fighting, hazing, theft, vandalism, criminal behavior, distribution of controlled substances, serious harassment or threats) draw immediate suspension, removal for the remainder of the season or longer, referral to school or legal authorities, and loss of awards, honors and leadership roles. Parent/guardian notification is required for Levels II-IV. The accompanying percentage-based suspension framework sets Level I at 0% (coach-managed), Level II at 10-20% of contests (typically 1 contest), Level III at 20-40% of contests and must meet or exceed MHSAA minimums, and Level IV at removal covering 50-100% of the season. The Athletic Director has final authority on athletic eligibility decisions; athletic suspensions may carry from one season to the next, including into the subsequent school year.

The final section, headed Section XIV but listed in the table of contents as Section XV, sets appeal procedures for violations of Sections V-XII. An appeal must be initiated in writing to the building principal and/or building athletic coordinator within five (5) school days of the date the discipline was communicated; a meeting including the student and coach, and possibly the parent/guardian, is convened within two (2) school days; a written decision upholding, modifying or revoking the action issues within two (2) school days. Further appeal goes in writing to the district Director of Athletics within two (2) school days of the building-level decision. Appeals concerning eligibility, transfer rules, or MHSAA regulation violations are submitted through the school athletic coordinator or district director of athletics to the MHSAA, follow a separate process, and are final and binding at the state level.

2026_349_february_2026_financial_stateme.paragraph: Troy School District unaudited statements of revenues and expenditures for the period July 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026 were presented to the Board of Education on April 21, 2026, covering the General Fund, Consolidated Debt Service Funds, four special revenue funds, the Sinking Fund, and two capital projects funds. General Fund actual revenues of $108,803,003 trailed actual expenditures of $110,100,357, producing revenues under expenditures of $(1,297,354) against an approved budgeted shortfall of $(3,739,630). The 2023 Capital Projects Fund (423) recorded $34,663,139 in expenditures with no revenue posted.

Across the eight-month reporting period, the General Fund shows expenditure running ahead of revenue, a pattern typical of the school-aid payment calendar. Taken together, the nine-month statements show the General Fund still running expenditures ahead of revenues but with a much smaller actual gap than the full-year budgeted shortfall, driven by state aid receipts that remain a fraction of the annual State Sources budget while local property tax collections have largely landed. Debt service and sinking fund collections are far ahead of the corresponding disbursements because principal and most capital payments fall later in the fiscal year. The Troy Preschool, Community Service, Sinking, and Consolidated Debt Service funds all report positive actual results; the Troy Career Center and Food Service funds report negative actual results; and both capital projects funds report expenditures with no revenue recognized.
